/-!

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Open coloring axiom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/open_coloring_axiom)

This file uses Todorčević's version of the open coloring axiom.
-/

namespace OpenColoringAxiom

/--
Todorčević's open coloring axiom (OCA). For every set `X` of real numbers and every
symmetric open coloring of the pairs from `X` into white and black, either there is an
uncountable white-homogeneous subset, or `X` is a countable union of black-homogeneous subsets.
-/
def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (white : Set (X × X)),
    SetRel.IsSymm white →
    (∀ x, (x, x) ∉ white) →
    IsOpen white →
    (∃ H : Set X, ¬H.Countable ∧ H.Pairwise fun x y ↦ (x, y) ∈ white) ∨
      ∃ pieces : ℕ → Set X,
        (⋃ n, pieces n) = Set.univ ∧
        ∀ n, (pieces n).Pairwise fun x y ↦ (x, y) ∉ white

/--
Is the open coloring axiom consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here `OCA` is Todorčević's open coloring axiom, and `Cardinal.continuum` denotes
$2^{\aleph_0}$. Thus the proposition on the right is OCA together with
$\aleph_2 < 2^{\aleph_0}$.

**Formalization caveat (consistency placeholder).** The question asks for relative consistency
over ZFC, namely $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}) \to
\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{OCA}+\aleph_2<2^{\aleph_0})$. Lean operates inside a
single fixed model of its set theory, and Mathlib does not provide a syntactic first-order theory
of ZFC with which to express this statement directly. Following the repository's convention for
such questions, `answer(sorry)` records the unknown consistency answer, while the right-hand side
records the axioms intended to hold in the putative model.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom : answer(sorry) ↔
    (OCA ∧ Cardinal.aleph 2 < Cardinal.continuum) := by
  sorry

end OpenColoringAxiom

namespace OpenColoringAxiom

/--
Todorčević's open coloring axiom. For a set `X` of reals and a symmetric open coloring
of its distinct pairs as white or black, either there is an uncountable set all of whose
pairs are white, or `X` is a countable union of sets all of whose pairs are black.

Here `white` is the white relation on the subtype `X`, with the product of its subspace
topology. It is irreflexive because only distinct pairs are colored. Its complement on
distinct pairs is the black relation. `Set.Pairwise` also restricts its condition to
distinct elements.
-/
def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (white : Set (X × X)),
    IsOpen white →
    (∀ x : X, (x, x) ∉ white) →
    (∀ x y : X, (x, y) ∈ white ↔ (y, x) ∈ white) →
    (∃ H : Set X, ¬ H.Countable ∧ H.Pairwise fun x y ↦ (x, y) ∈ white) ∨
      ∃ H : ℕ → Set X, (⋃ n, H n) = Set.univ ∧
        ∀ n, (H n).Pairwise fun x y ↦ (x, y) ∉ white

/--
Is OCA (Todorčević's open coloring axiom) consistent with
$2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$? More precisely, the question asks whether
$\operatorname{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC})$ implies
$\operatorname{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC} + \mathsf{OCA} + \aleph_2 < 2^{\aleph_0})$.

statement about models of ZFC. Lean operates inside a single fixed model and the repository
has no syntactic first-order ZFC theory with which to state that assertion directly.

cardinal inequality in Lean's fixed model. It must not be read as asserting that fixed-model

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Open coloring axiom

Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here OCA is Todorčević's open coloring axiom, the version spelled out in the *Statement* section
of the Wikipedia article: for every set of reals $X$ and every colouring of the pairs of distinct
elements of $X$ in black and white such that the set of white pairs is open, either $X$ has an
uncountable subset all of whose pairs are white, or $X$ is a countable union of sets all of whose
pairs are black. OCA follows from the proper forcing axiom, hence is consistent with ZFC, and it
implies that the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ (the least size of an unbounded family in Baire
space) equals $\aleph_2$ [To89]; in particular OCA implies $2^{\aleph_0} \ge \aleph_2$, and all
known models of OCA satisfy $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_2$. Whether OCA is consistent with
$2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$ is open [Mo10]. (For the older Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version of the
axiom the analogous question was answered positively by Gilton and Neeman [GN22], who obtained
a model of it with $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_3$.)

## Formalization notes

- **Version of OCA.** We formalize Todorčević's OCA, for subsets of $\mathbb R$, exactly as in
  the *Statement* section of the Wikipedia article. The white pairs of a colouring are encoded as
  a `SimpleGraph` on `X` whose adjacency set is open in `X × X`.
- **Consistency.** The question asks for the *consistency* of OCA with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$.
  Lean has no syntactic theory ZFC to state consistency about, so, following the convention of
  `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`, the statement records the conjunction
  `OCA ∧ ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠` behind an `answer(sorry)` placeholder. See the docstring of
  `open_coloring_axiom`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Open coloring axiom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/open_coloring_axiom)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [To89] Todorčević, S., [*Partition problems in topology*](https://archive.org/details/partitionproblem0000todo).
  Contemporary Mathematics 84, American Mathematical Society (1989).
- [Mo10] Moore, J. T., [*The proper forcing axiom*](https://www.math.cornell.edu/~justin/Ftp/ICM.pdf).
  Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM 2010), Vol. II, 3–29.
- [GN22] Gilton, T. and Neeman, I., *Abraham–Rubin–Shelah open colorings and a large continuum*.
  J. Math. Log. 22 (2022).
-/

open Cardinal Function

namespace OpenColoringAxiom

/--
**The open coloring axiom** (Todorčević's OCA).

Let $X \subseteq \mathbb R$ and colour each pair of distinct elements of $X$ either white or
black, so that the set of white pairs is open in $X \times X$. Then either
* $X$ has an uncountable subset all of whose pairs are white, or
* $X$ can be partitioned into countably many subsets, each of which has all its pairs black.

The white pairs are recorded as a simple graph `G` on `X` (a symmetric, irreflexive relation,
i.e. a set of unordered pairs of distinct points); `G.Adj x y` means that the pair $\{x, y\}$ is
white. The openness hypothesis is that `{(x, y) | G.Adj x y}` is open in `X × X`, where `X`
carries the subspace topology of $\mathbb R$. A white-homogeneous set is a clique of `G` and a
black-homogeneous set is an independent set of `G`. The countable partition is given by a
pairwise disjoint sequence `f : ℕ → Set X` of independent sets covering `X` (some of which may
be empty, so finite partitions are included).
-/
def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (G : SimpleGraph X), IsOpen {p : X × X | G.Adj p.1 p.2} →
    (∃ s : Set X, ¬ s.Countable ∧ G.IsClique s) ∨
    (∃ f : ℕ → Set X, Pairwise (Disjoint on f) ∧ (∀ n, G.IsIndepSet (f n)) ∧
      ⋃ n, f n = Set.univ)

/--
Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here `𝔠 = 2 ^ ℵ₀` is the cardinality of the continuum, so `ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠` is the statement
$2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$.

**Formalization caveat (consistency placeholder).** The question is *meta-theoretic*: it asks
whether ZFC + OCA + $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$ has a model, i.e. whether
$\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC})$ implies
$\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2)$.
Lean works inside a single fixed model of its foundations and has no syntactic first-order
theory ZFC available, so consistency cannot be expressed directly. Following the convention used
elsewhere in this repository (see `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`), we record
the question as an `answer(sorry)` placeholder for the conjunction `OCA ∧ ℵ_ 2 < 𝔠` itself.
A proof of `answer(False)` would show that OCA refutes $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$, i.e. a negative
answer to the question; a positive answer can only be established meta-theoretically (by a
forcing construction), not as a theorem of Lean, since OCA is independent of ZFC.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom : answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ (ℵ_ 2 : Cardinal.{0}) < 𝔠) := by
  sorry

/- ## Sanity checks for `OCA` -/

/-- The colouring in which every pair is white is an admissible open colouring: the set of
white pairs `{(x, y) | x ≠ y}` is open in `X × X`. Hence the openness hypothesis of `OCA` is
satisfiable by a colouring other than the all-black one. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom.test.top_isOpen (X : Set ℝ) :
    IsOpen {p : X × X | (⊤ : SimpleGraph X).Adj p.1 p.2} := by
  simp only [SimpleGraph.top_adj]
  exact isOpen_ne_fun continuous_fst continuous_snd

/-- For the all-white colouring of an uncountable $X \subseteq \mathbb R$, the first alternative
of `OCA` holds: $X$ itself is an uncountable white-homogeneous set. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom.test.top_uncountable (X : Set ℝ) (hX : ¬ X.Countable) :
    ∃ s : Set X, ¬ s.Countable ∧ (⊤ : SimpleGraph X).IsClique s :=
  ⟨Set.univ, fun h => hX (Set.countable_univ_iff.mp h).to_set, fun _ _ _ _ hxy => hxy⟩

/-- For a countable $X \subseteq \mathbb R$ and any colouring, the second alternative of `OCA`
holds: $X$ is partitioned into countably many singletons, which are trivially
black-homogeneous. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom.test.countable (X : Set ℝ) (hX : X.Countable) (G : SimpleGraph X) :
    ∃ f : ℕ → Set X, Pairwise (Disjoint on f) ∧ (∀ n, G.IsIndepSet (f n)) ∧
      ⋃ n, f n = Set.univ := by
  have : Countable X := hX.to_subtype
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := Countable.exists_injective_nat X
  refine ⟨fun n => e ⁻¹' {n}, fun m n hmn => ?_, fun n x hx y hy hxy => ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Set.disjoint_left.mpr fun x hx hx' => hmn (hx.symm.trans hx')
  · exact absurd (he (hx.trans hy.symm)) hxy
  · exact Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨e x, rfl⟩

end OpenColoringAxiom

/-!
# Open coloring axiom

The open coloring axiom (OCA) is an axiom about colorings of the pairs of a set of reals.
Two versions were introduced, by Abraham, Rubin and Shelah [ARS85] and by Todorčević [To89].
The version spelled out in the Wikipedia article, and formalized here, is Todorčević's.

**Todorčević's open coloring axiom.** Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and color each pair of
distinct elements of $X$ either black or white, in such a way that the set of white pairs is open
(in the topology on pairs inherited from $X \times X$). Then either
- $X$ has an uncountable subset all of whose pairs are white, or
- $X$ is the union of countably many subsets, each of which has all of its pairs black.

Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems asks: *Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with
$2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?* Todorčević's OCA implies that the bounding number $\mathfrak{b}$
equals $\aleph_2$, hence $2^{\aleph_0} \geq \aleph_2$; it is open whether the continuum can be
larger than $\aleph_2$ in a model of OCA.

## Formalization notes

- **Colorings as graphs.** A black/white coloring of the pairs of $X$ is recorded as a
  `SimpleGraph X`, whose edges are the white pairs. White-homogeneous sets are cliques
  (`SimpleGraph.IsClique`) and black-homogeneous sets are independent sets
  (`SimpleGraph.IsIndepSet`). The openness hypothesis is that the adjacency relation is an open
  subset of `X × X`, where `X` carries the subspace topology of `ℝ`.
- **Countable partitions.** "A partition of $X$ into countably many black-homogeneous sets" is
  recorded as a cover of $X$ by an `ℕ`-indexed family of independent sets. This is equivalent:
  a subset of an independent set is independent, so any such cover can be refined to a partition,
  and a finite or countable family can be re-indexed by `ℕ` (repeating sets or using `∅`).
- **Consistency placeholder.** The question is a *relative consistency* question
  (does $\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$ have a model?). Lean works inside
  one fixed model of its set theory and Mathlib has no syntactic first-order theory of ZFC, so

  mathematical content is the model-theoretic statement
  $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}) \to \mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2)$.

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/open_coloring_axiom)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [ARS85] Abraham, U., Rubin, M., Shelah, S., *On the consistency of some partition theorems for

-/

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Open coloring axiom

Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here OCA is Todorčević's open coloring axiom: for every set of reals $X$ and every
coloring of the pairs of distinct elements of $X$ in two colors, white and black, with the set
of white pairs open, either $X$ has an uncountable subset all of whose pairs are white, or $X$
is a countable union of sets all of whose pairs are black. This is the version spelled out in
the Wikipedia article and the version for which the question is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Open coloring axiom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/open_coloring_axiom)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [To89] Todorčević, S., *Partition problems in topology*, Contemporary Mathematics 84,
  American Mathematical Society (1989).
- [Mo11] Moore, J. T., *Logic and foundations: the proper forcing axiom*, Proceedings of the
  ICM 2010, Vol. II, 3–29.
- [Ca13] Carotenuto, G., *An introduction to OCA*, lecture notes (2013).
-/

open Cardinal
open scoped Cardinal

namespace OpenColoringAxiom

/--
**Todorčević's open coloring axiom (OCA).**

Let $X$ be a set of reals and suppose that each pair of distinct elements of $X$ is colored
either white or black, in such a way that the set of white pairs is open in $X \times X$.
Then either
* $X$ has an uncountable subset $Y$ such that every pair of distinct elements of $Y$ is white, or
* $X$ is the union of countably many subsets $X_n$ such that every pair of distinct elements of
  the same $X_n$ is black.

The coloring is encoded by its set of white pairs `W : Set (X × X)`, which is required to be
symmetric (pairs are unordered) and open in the product of the subspace topologies on `X`.
A pair `{x, y}` with `x ≠ y` is white when `(x, y) ∈ W` and black otherwise; the diagonal plays
no role. Since every subset of a black-homogeneous set is black-homogeneous, a countable cover
`f : ℕ → Set X` is equivalent to a countable partition. As noted in the Wikipedia article, OCA
can equivalently be stated for arbitrary separable metric spaces in place of subsets of
$\mathbb{R}$.
-/
def OCA : Prop :=
  ∀ (X : Set ℝ) (W : Set (X × X)), IsOpen W → (∀ p ∈ W, p.swap ∈ W) →
    (∃ Y : Set X, ¬ Y.Countable ∧ ∀ x ∈ Y, ∀ y ∈ Y, x ≠ y → (x, y) ∈ W) ∨
    (∃ f : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ f n, ∀ y ∈ f n, x ≠ y → (x, y) ∉ W) ∧ ⋃ n, f n = Set.univ)

/--
Is OCA (the open coloring axiom) consistent with $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$?

Here OCA is Todorčević's open coloring axiom `OCA`, the version spelled out in the Wikipedia
article. This is the version for which the question is open: OCA implies that the bounding
number $\mathfrak{b}$ equals $\aleph_2$, so the question is whether the continuum
$\mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$ can be larger than $\aleph_2$ in the presence of OCA. (The
Abraham–Rubin–Shelah version of the axiom is known to be consistent with
$2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_3$ by work of Gilton and Neeman.)

**Formalization caveat (consistency placeholder).** The question is a *relative consistency*
statement: it asks whether $\mathrm{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC})$ implies
$\mathrm{Con}(\mathsf{ZFC} + \mathrm{OCA} + 2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2)$, that is, whether there is
a model of ZFC in which both OCA and $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_2$ hold. Lean works inside a single
fixed model of its set theory and Mathlib has no syntactic first-order theory ZFC, so
consistency cannot be expressed directly. Following the repository precedent
(`erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`), we record the problem as an `answer(sorry)`
consistency placeholder whose right-hand side is the conjunction
$\mathrm{OCA} \wedge \aleph_2 < 2^{\aleph_0}$ that a witnessing model must satisfy.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem open_coloring_axiom : answer(sorry) ↔ (OCA ∧ (ℵ_ 2 : Cardinal.{0}) < 𝔠) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check for the definition of `OCA`: the dichotomy holds for every countable set of reals
$X$ and every set of white pairs $W$, because $X$ is the countable union of its singletons and
a singleton contains no pair of distinct points.
-/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem OCA_dichotomy_of_countable (X : Set ℝ) (hX : X.Countable) (W : Set (X × X)) :
    (∃ Y : Set X, ¬ Y.Countable ∧ ∀ x ∈ Y, ∀ y ∈ Y, x ≠ y → (x, y) ∈ W) ∨
    (∃ f : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ f n, ∀ y ∈ f n, x ≠ y → (x, y) ∉ W) ∧ ⋃ n, f n = Set.univ) := by
  right
  have : Countable X := hX.to_subtype
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty X with hempty | hne
  · refine ⟨fun _ => ∅, fun n x hx => absurd hx (Set.notMem_empty x), ?_⟩
    exact Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => (IsEmpty.false x).elim
  · obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := exists_surjective_nat X
    refine ⟨fun n => {g n}, fun n x hx y hy hxy => ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact absurd (hx.trans hy.symm) hxy
    · exact Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => by
        obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := hg x
        exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨n, rfl⟩

end OpenColoringAxiom
